subject: Post-discovery: ClinicCo long-context fit & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Turner <emma@clinicco.com>, Jacob Li <j.li@clinicco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-discovery: ClinicCo long-context fit & next steps

Hi Emma / Jacob — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from discovery:
- Primary use case: ingest multi-page clinical notes (avg 3–8 pages, many with threaded annotations) to produce structured visit summaries and problem lists; must preserve temporal order across visit sections.
- Key constraints: frequent long histories (>20k tokens), PII handling + retention rules, and requirement for >95% fidelity on critical sections (meds, allergies).
- Success metric: extraction + summarization fidelity measured against clinician-reviewed gold set; latency target for interactive UI < 2s median for 1k-token requests (batching allowed for bulk jobs).

Risks we called out: truncation of trailing context (notes with appended labs/transcripts), hallucination in synthesized problem lists when context is partially dropped, and cost at scale if naive generation per note is used.

Recommended immediate plan (attachments + links included):
1) Short pilot eval (2 weeks): run 200 real notes through our long-window eval harness to measure truncation and summary fidelity. We attach a starter prompt set and the benchmark CSV with synthetic boundary cases.
2) Model candidates: we suggest testing a mid-sized open LLM variant with extended KV-cache (we'll propose model variants in follow-up) + a quantized 8-bit variant to measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
3) Eval metrics: ROUGE/EM for extraction targets, clinician pass/fail for critical sections, and token-coverage analysis to detect where truncation happens.
4) Data handling: we propose a scoped dataset transfer (SFTP or signed URL) and will run in our isolated private tenancy for the pilot.

Attachments: prompt-sets-clinicco-v1.jsonl (sample prompts), clinicco-long-context-benchmarks.csv (case list), mutual-action-plan.docx (M.A.P). Also linking: https://drive.google.com/cl/clinicco-longcontext-benchmarks and https://share.redwood.ai/evals/CLINICCO-2026-01

Next steps / asks from you:
- Confirm pilot scope and whether we can get a curated 200-note set by Jan 23.
- Are there additional compliance items we should include up front (e.g., named auditors, specific retention windows)?
- Availability for a 30-min pilot kickoff next Tue or Wed (Jan 20/21).

Happy to adjust — thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Tessa — thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications before we lock the pilot: 

1) Data/sample set: we can provide the 200-note set but we need to strip direct identifiers first; would a hashed-id + date window work for your eval harness? We can include an internal mapping file under NDA if needed.
2) PII & retention: we have a 7-year retention policy but would prefer the pilot data to be wiped from non-production systems after 30 days. Can you confirm wipe/retention controls and whether the private tenancy supports short TTLs?
3) Prompt examples: the prompt set looks reasonable — could you include one example that demonstrates how you handle context windows that exceed the model limit (e.g., do you summarize older segments and include them as condensed context)?

Also, can you share the expected S3/SFTP format and a drive link for the eval results so our team can review as they come in? We are available for kickoff on Wed Jan 21 after 10:00 AM PT.

—Emma

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Emma Turner <emma@clinicco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: ClinicCo long-context fit & next steps

Emma — quick responses to your items and proposal details we can use in the kickoff: 

1) Data / PII & retention: yes, hashed-id + date window works. For the pilot we recommend the private tenancy with a 30-day TTL on all evaluation artifacts; we'll provide an auditable wipe log. We will also sign an MPUA clause for the pilot as requested.

2) Handling > model limit contexts: we have two approaches to test in the pilot (both are included as prompt variants in the attached prompt-sets):
   a) Sliding-window summarization: chunk older sections > N tokens, generate condensed summaries, and include condensed tokens as a prefix to the active window. Best for preserving signal across long histories but requires evaluation of compression fidelity.
   b) Hybrid prefix-KV strategy: store embeddings + lightweight metadata for older segments and retrieve / concatenate compressed context only on disambiguation signals (e.g., when extraction fields reference prior events). This reduces token cost but adds retrieval complexity.

3) Model recommendations for the pilot (tradeoffs):
   - Candidate A (low-latency): Redwood-Open-XS-extkv (optimized for extended KV cache; lower memory footprint) — good for UI paths, expected median latency ~1.1s on a 1k-token window.
   - Candidate B (higher-fidelity): Redwood-Open-L-mid (larger context native support, better summarization fidelity; cost ~2.3x Candidate A).
   - Candidate C (cost-optimized): Redwood-Open-L-quant8 (8-bit quantized; slightly higher hallucination risk in edge cases, but cost-per-token reduced ~45%).

Benchmarks & artifacts we will share in the kickoff: the CSV contains boundary-case labels, the eval harness will produce per-note fidelity and truncation heatmaps, and we will attach an initial set of clinician pass/fail evaluations in Drive. Links: https://share.redwood.ai/evals/CLINICCO-2026-01 (live) and internal notes at https://drive.google.com/cl/clinicco-longcontext-benchmarks

4) Canary / rollout suggestion: run the pilot on 200 notes, then a 1-week canary of 1,000 notes targeting the most common templates. If the canary shows <2% regression on critical sections and acceptable latency, we can scale to prod.

I've attached a short one-pager summarizing the approach (clinicco-eval-summaries.pdf) and the prompt variants. Will present this during kickoff if helpful.

—Rishi
